The 2027 All Progressives Congress governorship candidate in Ogun State and senator representing Ogun West, Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, has warned against attacks on APC candidates and the destruction of their campaign materials, including billboards and posters. Adeola said the ruling party would no longer tolerate political violence, destruction of campaign materials and other acts of intimidation against its candidates and supporters. The senator, according to a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Media, Kayode Odunaro, on Sunday, stated this during the inauguration of 357 ward and local government coordinators of the APC across the state in Yewa South Local Government Area. The inauguration and distribution of vehicles were witnessed by the Ogun State Deputy Governor, Noimot Salako-Oyedele; former deputy governors, Alhaja Salmot Badru and Segun Adesegun; the Minister of State for Health, Dr Kunle Salako; Senator Lekan Mustapha; the Director-General of the Ogun State APC Presidential and Gubernatorial Campaign Council, Gboyega Nasiru Isiaka; among others. The governorship candidate urged political actors and their supporters to abide by the rule and embrace peaceful political participation as political activities gathered momentum ahead of the 2027 elections. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “I condemn the reported attacks on APC candidates and campaign materials. It should be noted that no individual or political group has a monopoly of violence. “Nobody has a monopoly of violence. Stoning candidates and their supporters, and destroying APC candidates’ posters and billboards, will no longer be tolerated. Nobody is above the law,” he said. The senator stressed that attacks on President Bola Tinubu, Vice-President Kashim Shettima and other APC candidates must stop, warning that the party would not condone further acts of political aggression. 2027: Katsina gov promises more development, seeks APC victory Military killed over 15,000 terrorists in three years – APC PCC State police: Senate sets November 17 deadline for four states Adeola explained that the number of ward coordinators had been increased from 236 to 357 following an assessment of the peculiarities and organisational needs of various wards across the state. He charged the newly inaugurated coordinators to work round the clock to strengthen the party’s grassroots structures, warning that anyone found engaging in activities capable of causing disaffection or undermining the APC would be removed. The senator also cautioned the beneficiaries against personalising the vehicles and motorcycles distributed to them, stressing that the items were provided strictly for party mobilisation and official assignments. He disclosed that plans were underway to provide Closed User Group telephone lines to the coordinators to improve communication and coordination across the state. Adeola, who said the inauguration marked the end of his tour of Ogun State’s 20 local government areas, added that concerns and memoranda submitted by communities during the engagements would be incorporated into his economic blueprint and manifesto, tagged ITESIWAJU. He expressed confidence that the expanded grassroots structure would help the APC achieve its target of delivering two million votes for President Tinubu in the forthcoming presidential election. Taiwo Bankole
